Put your jobs in your own order and see them in a compact list, go true black on OLED screens and let the accent take your system's colour. The sign-in page has a new look, the lists sort, filter and search from their own headings, a backup of a folder people keep working in stays green, and previews against an FTP server on a phone work again.

## ✨ Added

- **You can put the jobs in your own order.** Each job has a small handle: drag it with the mouse and the other jobs make room, or press Alt and an arrow key on the job. On the phone, hold a job and drag it. The order is saved in `arrowloop.json`, new jobs go to the end, and the overview, the job list and the Job filter in History, Trash and Conflicts all follow it. Until you move a job, the jobs stay in alphabetical order and the file isn't touched. Thanks to @leonp5 for asking in #122.
- **The job list has a compact view.** Choose between Cards and Compact under Job list in Settings › Look, and on the phone under Appearance in Settings. Compact shows one row per job with its colour, name, status, last run, Run now and More, and a click on the row opens the job. Each device remembers its choice, and moving jobs works in both views.
- **OLED puts the dark look on true black.** The switch sits under Design in Settings › Look, and on the phone under Appearance in Settings. It counts whenever the dark look shows, also when Design follows the system, so the screen goes black at night without another tap. Each browser and each phone keeps its own choice, since an OLED phone and an LCD laptop want different things. Thanks to @leonp5 for asking in #123.
- **The accent can take your system's colour.** A swatch with a wand stands first in the accent row wherever the system has a colour of its own: Material You from Android 12 on the phone, the accent colour of Windows, macOS or Linux in the desktop app, and the system colour in Firefox and Safari. Chrome and the browsers built on it don't share it, so there the swatch isn't shown. The choice is saved as the system's colour rather than as a hex code, so each device paints its own, and ArrowLoop picks it up again when you come back from the system's settings. Thanks to @leonp5 for asking in #124.
- **Other programs can add a job with `POST /api/jobs`.** Put a long random token in the new optional `ARROWLOOP_API_TOKEN` variable, in the advanced view of the Unraid template, and enter the same token in the other program, such as CannonCommander. It sends the token in the `X-ArrowLoop-Token` header. The token opens the job list and adding a job, never the settings or the trash, and a wrong token is always refused. A name that's taken gets a 409 and the existing job stays as it is. `before` and `after` are dropped, as with every save from the interface.
- **A job added this way runs on its schedule like any other,** and a mirror deletes at its destination, so keep the token as safe as the password. Without the variable nothing changes. Without a password, the job routes stay open to anyone who reaches the port, as they always were, so set one as well. `docs/installing.md` has an example.

## 🎨 Design

- **The lists in History, Trash, Conflicts and Anomalies sort, filter and search from their own headings.** A click on a heading sorts, the ▾ beside it filters, and typing in the list, or Ctrl+F, opens a search that floats over the list until Escape closes it. On a touch screen a magnifier at the end of the headings opens it. A filter or a search that narrows a list says so above it, with Show everything to undo it. A line under the headings explains all this on hover, and once by itself on the first visit. The Filter and Search buttons over History are gone.
- **A job's Files touched filters and searches from the head of its list too.**
- **Closed findings live in History,** as a third view beside Runs and Files with the findings closed in the last thirty days, filtered by severity and job from the headings. Anomalies shows only what is open, without the Open or closed selector, and leads to History when something was closed. The phone app does the same.
- **The columns in History and a job's Files touched can be moved and widened,** as in KnightLoader: drag a heading and the columns make room while you drag, drag the line at any column's edge to change its width, and double-click the line for the original width. Every line keeps to its column on one line, cut at the end. Each list keeps its arrangement in the browser.
- **A heading's filter opens under its ▾ over the dimmed and blurred page,** like every other window, and never over the sidebar or below the page. A long list of choices scrolls inside it and stands lower. Its choices stand side by side where they fit and under each other where not.
- **Trash and Conflicts count what they hold in tiles,** like Anomalies: the trash in three for all of it and each side, the conflicts in four for all of them and each kind. A tile shows its part alone, and the ▾ at the Job heading narrows the list to one job, however many jobs there are. The phone app has the same chips and the job filter in the list's head.
- **The three answers to a conflict stand in the order of the sides:** keep the left version, keep both, keep the right version, on the web and on the phone, and the answers for all of them under More follow the same order.
- **The phone app's History sorts and filters from the headings of its list.** A tap on a heading sorts, its ▾ opens the filter, and the magnifier at the end of the row opens the search. The Filter, Sort and Search buttons above it are gone.
- **Every button takes the accent when the pointer or the keyboard reaches it.** A grey button mixes a little of the accent into its ground and turns its symbol to the accent, while its words keep their colour. A button that is a symbol alone turns the symbol. On the phone a grey button does the same while your finger is on it. Under rainbow every button lights up in a colour of its own, counting through the palette in the order the buttons stand.
- **Each side of a job starts with where the folder is:** this phone or one of your targets, as buttons. Then you type or pick the folder inside it, and the folder picker stays within that target. Jobs are saved the same way as before.
- **Advanced in a job's settings is a button with a ground of its own,** like every other button with words, so it no longer reads as a heading.
- **The F-Droid button in Settings › Apps wears F-Droid's logo as GlimStone carries it,** flat in its own greens and blue, with the eyes still cut out.
- **Check for updates in Settings › Info wears the sync symbol,** as in KnightLoader. The cloud stays with fetching an update.
- **A finding on the Anomalies page has no coloured edge any more,** on the web and on the phone. Its badge says how bad it is.
- **Sizes stand at the start of their column,** with their heading, in History, a job's Files touched and the trash.
- **The duplicate search's buttons say what they do:** Find duplicates on the left side and Find duplicates on the right side.
- **The sign-in page has a new look,** the same as in the other apps: the ArrowLoop logo and name at the top, the labels above the fields and every button as wide as the card. The cursor is already in the password field, Sign in waits until you type, and a wrong password or code gives it a little shake while the card keeps its place. Passkeys, the second step and Forgot password? work as before. The button now says Sign in, and its partner in the menu Sign out.
- **ArrowLoop follows GlimStone 4.2.6.** While you hold a job, a settings tile or a column heading to move it, the others move a little so you can see they can be moved too: jobs tremble gently, tiles and headings wiggle. A dragged column heading changes places as soon as its front edge passes the middle of the next one, so even a wide column gets back to the front. Blue, Red, Purple, Orange and Magenta carry dark text and glyphs instead of white, which was hard to read on them, in the accent and in the rainbow alike. A colour you mix yourself gets text that stays readable on every card too. Under OLED the cards stand on black without a ring around them, and the OLED switch says why it waits while Light is chosen.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The README compares ArrowLoop with FolderSync and luckyBackup as well.** The same table is in `docs/comparison.md`.
- **The README's download buttons sit under Server, Desktop and Android titles,** and a new F-Droid button leads to ArrowLoop's listing there.
- **The web interface and the phone app are built with the latest minor releases of their dependencies,** and the phone app's build tools use glob 14 and minimatch 11, which close two advisories. Nothing of them ships in the app.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **A preview or run against an FTP server on a phone no longer fails with "Maximum login limit has been reached".** ArrowLoop opens at most 4 connections to an FTP target unless its concurrency setting says otherwise. When the server still turns a login away, ArrowLoop tries again with 2 and then 1 and remembers the number for that server. It keeps a job's transfers below that, logs out after a test, a preview or a run, and says in plain words when a server is out of logins. Thanks to @antrixsamay for the report in #130.
- **The tabs of the phone app don't wait for a target that doesn't answer anymore.** The trash and conflict counts give up on such a target after a minute and read every job's conflicts side by side, and the app runs more requests to the engine at once, so switching tabs stays quick.
- **A second desktop copy started with its own `--config` opens on Linux every time.** Its single-instance name could start a part with a digit, which the session bus refuses, so about two starts in three failed.
- **A file that disappears from the source while a run is going no longer turns the run yellow.** A rotated log or a Git branch deleted meanwhile is gone by the next run anyway, so History lists it as disappeared before it was copied and the run carries on. A copy the destination refuses is still reported.
- **A file that is written to while it is copied no longer stops the run or warns about it.** A growing log, or a session file that gets a line while it is copied, is left for the next run without recording the pair, and the next run sends it again rather than taking the copy it left behind for a conflict. An edit made on the far side since is still one. Only a file that is caught like this in three runs in a row is reported, so one that never settles still shows. A pair that disagrees without having been touched still stops the run.
- **A mirror to a Windows folder replaces read-only files again.** Git writes its objects and commit graphs read-only, and a job that carries file attributes copies that along. The next change to such a file failed on every run with access denied, because Windows refuses to rename a new copy over a read-only file, so a backup of a Git working copy ended every run with a warning.
- **A job on the phone's folders asks for file access before it runs.** Without all-files access, Android shows ArrowLoop the phone's folders with every other app's files hidden, so a run found nothing to copy and still said it was done. Saving or starting such a job now explains this and opens the settings page. A run that can't read its folders, scheduled ones included, ends as an error that says why.
- **The phone app keeps the language you chose.** The engine refused to store it, so every start fell back to the phone's language. The app also waits for the stored language before it draws its screens, which stops a crash on some cold starts.
- **The hint that no cloud or server is connected shows again** when only Apps or Android/data are set up, since both live on the phone itself.
- **The keyboard doesn't cover the field you're typing in anymore.** ArrowLoop targets Android 16, so it's drawn edge to edge, and Android stopped shrinking the window for the keyboard. A field near the end of a page, like a new target's password, stayed hidden behind it. Every page now makes room for the keyboard and scrolls the field you tapped into view.
- **Two changes to the settings at the same moment both stick.** Each save reads the file, edits it and writes it back, so two at once could lose one of them. They wait for each other now.
- **Desktop and phone builds use Go 1.27.3, which fixes a crypto/x509 flaw (GO-2026-6809).**
- **The engine uses klauspost/compress 1.20.2, which fixes a crash on some two-block compressed frames (GO-2026-6865).**

## 🌐 Translations

- **Every new text is in all 42 languages.**
